title: Interpolation Is Not Invariance: Pair Count Is Not Coverage in Transformation Audits
abstract: arXiv:2609.14870v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Counting equivalent pairs is a common way to report transformation-audit coverage, but it can substantially overstate the constraints imposed by an audit: pairs generated from the same semantic object are correlated, and complete orbit graphs contain algebraically redundant edges. We therefore distinguish four complementary quantities---edge count $m$, effective contrast rank $s$, population support rank $r$, and graph spectral gap $\eta$---and characterize their roles in audit coverage and deployment reliability. Under a rank-$r$ Gaussian contrast model, a population-invariant calibrated reader exists exactly when the anchor has a component in $\ker T$. When an audit has rank $s < r$, its unobserved risk is $R^\star/U$, with $U \sim \operatorname{Beta}((r-s)/2,s/2)$; when $s \ge r$, exact calibrated interpolation is infeasible. tldr: 该论文揭示变换审计中的对计数会因语义对象相关性和轨道图冗余边而严重夸大审计覆盖度，提出用边数、有效对比秩、总体支撑秩和图谱间隙四个互补量刻画审计覆盖度与部署可靠性，并给出未观测风险的精确分布刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that pair counts substantially overstate transformation-audit coverage due to correlated semantic objects and algebraically redundant orbit edges, distinguishing four complementary quantities—edge count, effective contrast rank, population support rank, and graph spectral gap—to characterize audit coverage and deployment reliability, with exact characterizations of unobserved risk.
